prompt: Use java.lang.reflect.Proxy to build a Greeter at runtime that logs each method name before delegating to the real implementation. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Proxy.newProxyInstance generates a class at runtime that implements the interfaces you list, and routes every call on it into a single InvocationHandler.invoke(proxy, method, args). That one method is your interception point: the Method parameter tells you which call arrived (method.getName()), and method.invoke(target, args) forwards it to the real object and returns its result. This is how logging, timing, and transaction wrappers are built without hand-writing a delegating class per interface -- the cost is that the compiler can no longer check the wrapper, so mistakes show up only at runtime.
hints: newProxyInstance needs three arguments: a class loader, `new Class<?>[] { Greeter.class }`, and your handler. It returns Object, so cast the result to Greeter.
The handler can be a lambda: `(proxy, method, args) -> { ... }` -- InvocationHandler has a single method.
Inside the handler, add method.getName() to the log FIRST, then `return method.invoke(target, args);` so the caller still gets the real answer.
